title: Packet-level function vector
hypothesis: One compact task function vector shared across all packet slots can encode slot-coupled functions with a better payload/quality point than a generic PTP packet latent, including the cost of private exceptions.
mirror_coordinate: rank-q task function vector m_t inferred from labeled support examples and shared over P=4 slots
logical_multiplicity: task-specific four-slot packet functions from a shared decoder; six aligned tasks plus two private exceptions

selection.method: secrets.randbelow over sorted eligible P0/UNTESTED IDs after exclusions
selection.exclusions: previously completed worker IDs and paused families listed in prior draw record

data.target: four continuous teacher outputs per context

development.selection_metric: choose the smallest q with mean Mirror normalized MSE <=1e-6; within that q choose ridge penalty with lowest mean MSE

success_gate: 3/3 fresh seeds meet Mirror MSE <=1.05x PTP and exact packet accuracy within 0.01; actual Mirror payload <=0.90x PTP; inference MAC proxy <=1.25x.
failure_gate: Quality gates pass but actual payload reduction is <10%, or either fresh quality gate fails.
boundaries: Task function codes are inferred from labeled support examples; no oracle target code is provided at inference beyond serialized code.
No natural-language, pretrained Transformer, hidden random packet mode, or capacity claim.
The function-vector method and generic PTP latent are matched in rank and basis by design.
